messages:
ashok: quick question 1: for private deployments are we leaning toward short-circuit CP->DP inside customer VPC or relay-mode via our regional proxy?

maria: short take: short-circuit = lower egress & fewer hops but larger customer ops + trust surface. relay = centralized auth/observability and easier rollouts.

kevin: perf numbers from last spike: relay avg RTT ~22ms (p95 ~48ms) for auth+config RPCs; direct-peering avg RTT ~8ms (p95 ~14ms).

olga: thanks. Aside from latency, short-circuit requires a small agent in-customer for cert negotiation, health checks, and fallback handling 1 lifecycle pain.

ashok: security: we must enforce ephemeral certs and mutual TLS. Prefer OIDC-based onetime bootstrap to avoid long-lived credentials.

olga: agreed, but rotation/rotation tooling becomes customer's responsibility or we offer managed KMS integration. Ops surface grows.

kevin: observability: relay gives unified tracing and sampling. Short-circuit needs local forwarders or remote exporters which customers may block. Add telemetry opt-in.

maria: propose three supported modes: relay (default), short-circuit (opt-in agent+peering), managed-relay-in-customer (we deploy relay into customer account). Each has different SLA and pricing.

tom: regulated customers (e.g., fintech) sometimes forbid egress. For them, managed-relay-in-customer or short-circuit w/o egress is required.

olga: interface contract for the agent: small gRPC surface, health endpoints, fetch-config, force-fallback, and a local socket for CP RPCs. Must fail open to relay.

maria: sketch of agent API and fallback semantics:
```
service AgentControl {
  rpc Heartbeat(HeartbeatReq) returns (HeartbeatResp);
  rpc FetchConfig(FetchReq) returns (Config);
  rpc ForceFallback(ForceReq) returns (Ack);
}
```

kevin: ephemeral cert flow: CP issues a boot token; agent performs OIDC challenge, exchanges for short-lived certs stored optionally in customer KMS. Use short TTLs and automatic rotation.

ashok: crucial: ability to remotely force fallback to relay within ~5s. Agent should accept signed CP commands and flip routing. Also periodic heartbeat so CP detects silence and auto-fallback.

maria: enumerate failure scenarios in followup RFC: network partition, cert compromise, CP region outage, agent compromise. For each, list mitigations and diagnostic signals.

olga: telemetry and logs must support PII masking. Provide a telemetry toggle in agent config because some customers block log egress.

kevin: throughput note: short-circuit reduces kernel hops but reduces central batching. For high-throughput tenants, add local batching inside agent to preserve cost & perf.

tom: I'll model pricing for 'short-circuit add-on' and managed-relay. Need expected extra-support hours and SLA.

maria: action items: 1) agent RPC spec (ashok+olga), 2) ephemeral cert + KMS integration design (kevin+ashok), 3) fallback semantics & probes (maria), 4) pricing/SLA tiers (tom). 2-week spike -> staging demo -> beta customers -> GA in ~3 months if no blockers.

ashok: I'll kick off the spike and include a minimal PoC that shows ForceFallback and heartbeats.

olga: I'll draft the agent wire-protocol and private hosted zone recommendation (prefer private hosted zone delegation over ENI-based IP routing for TLS/SNI continuity).

maria: conclusion: relay-mode stays GA default; short-circuit is opt-in advanced mode with guardrails, force-fallback, and telemetry controls. Filing RFC amendment and follow-up checklist. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: created INFRA-4821 assigned to @ashok for agent spike.
